children: Alnylam reported five-year HELIOS-B analyses: continuous vutrisiran was associated with 48% lower risk of death and recurrent cardiovascular events in the monotherapy population and 41% lower risk in the overall population versus delayed initiation. A 48-patient post hoc analysis found preserved exercise capacity versus placebo over two years.
Five-year results favor earlier, continuous treatment; the release gives no absolute event rates or prior-period comparison.
Recurrent CV event risk lower 50% and 41%
The reductions were in monotherapy and overall populations, respectively, versus delayed initiation.
Continuous vutrisiran plus tafamidis was associated with a 23% reduction versus tafamidis alone before later vutrisiran initiation.
Post hoc analysis of 48 patients found a difference versus placebo over two years; small sample limits breadth of the finding.
No new safety signals through 60 months
Supports the reported longer-term safety profile; the release provides no new safety concern.

This is a long-term clinical-data update for an already approved therapy, extending the HELIOS-B evidence beyond the previously reported 36-month results. Further commercial impact would depend on uptake and whether regulators or treatment guidelines act on the longer-term findings.
